get.description: The platform keys that sign restore certificates. No sign-in needed.

A restore certificate and whether its signature checks out. No sign-in
needed: give the link to an auditor, a client or an insurer.

post.description:
Finish linking a cloud account: the dashboard's callback page sends the
state and code the provider returned. Only the person who started the link
can finish it, and only once.

get.description:
Every instance you can reach, in every organization you work in or that a
partner lends to one of yours, with one health verdict each (FR-MON-008).
The signed-in user and the organizations they can switch between (FR-ACC-005).

patch.description: Save the signed-in user's own preferences, such as the dashboard language.

post.description: Create an organization. The caller becomes its owner.

patch.description:
Rename the organization. Owners can also require two-factor sign-in for all members
and change the data residency, which limits where new servers can be created.

post.description:
Create an API key (FR-API-003). The secret is returned this once.

The key acts with `role`, optionally narrowed to servers or instances, and
stops working if you stop being an owner or admin. Keys cannot delete
anything: destructive operations need a signed-in person.

delete.description: Revoke a key at once. It stays listed, marked revoked, for the audit trail.

get.description:
Connected assistants (FR-MCP-004): everyone's for owners and admins,
otherwise your own.

delete.description:
Disconnect an assistant: its next request is refused, and its tokens are
revoked at the OAuth server.

get.description:
The organization's SSH public key, created on first request and never
replaced silently. Run `setup_command` as root on the server: it creates
`ssh_user`, the user Odotify always attaches as, with this key and
passwordless sudo.
The organization's audit log, newest first, filterable as FR-AUD-003 requires.

parameters.description: Exact action, or a prefix ending in `.*`
parameters.name: action

schema.description: Exact action, or a prefix ending in `.*`
schema.title: Action

get.description: Recompute the hash chain to prove no audit row was altered or removed.

post.description:
Add your own S3, GCS, Azure or SFTP storage (FR-BAK-004).

Credentials are encrypted and only ever sent to your servers' agents. A
connection test runs from every active server; for SFTP, add the returned
public key to the account first, then run the test.

delete.description: Remove a destination no schedule uses. Archives already stored there are kept.

post.description: Write, read back and delete a test file from every active server (FR-BAK-006).

get.description:
Plan, billing standing, usage against the plan's limits and managed
backup storage so far this period (FR-BIL-002, FR-BIL-006).

post.description:
Cancel at the end of the paid period, or keep the plan after all. When it
ends the organization moves to the free plan; nothing is deleted.

Upgrade, downgrade or switch between monthly and yearly billing.

Upgrades and period changes are charged at once, prorated; downgrades are
credited on the next invoice. A smaller plan must hold what already runs.

Subscribe to a paid plan through Stripe Checkout. Send the user to `url`.

Any trial time left carries over: the card is saved now and charged when the
trial ends, unless `start_now`. Prices include VAT where it applies; business
customers in the EU can enter a VAT number for the reverse charge.

The Stripe customer portal: card, billing address, VAT number, invoices,
plan changes and cancellation.

get.description: The white-label profile: what clients see on the portal and in emails.

put.description:
Set the product name, colour, support contacts, the portal's own hostname
(CNAME it to the address shown) and the sender for client emails (verify it
with the DNS records shown). Needs the Agency plan.

post.description: Look again at the portal hostname and the sender domain's DNS records.

put.description: Upload the logo, the logo for dark backgrounds, or the favicon (256 KB at most).

post.description:
Link an AWS account (ADR 0021). Returns a CloudFormation template that
creates a role trusting Odotify with an external id made for this link.
Deploy it in your account, then send the role ARN to
PUT /cloud/aws/{credential_id}. Odotify never holds an AWS key of yours.

get.description: The template and external id of an AWS link again, to finish or redo it.

put.description:
Send the ARN of the role the template created. Odotify assumes it once to
check it, then the account can be used to create servers.

post.description:
Link an Azure subscription (ADR 0031). Returns Azure CLI commands that
add Odotify's Microsoft Entra app to your tenant, create a resource group
with a name made for this link, and give the app Contributor on that
resource group only. Run them, then send the subscription and tenant ids to
PUT /cloud/azure/{credential_id}. Odotify never holds a key of yours.

get.description: The setup commands of an Azure link again, to finish or redo it.

put.description:
Send the subscription and tenant ids the commands printed. Odotify signs
in to your tenant and reads the resource group once to check it, then the
subscription can be used to create servers.

post.description:
Save a Hetzner Cloud API token (read and write) so Odotify can create
servers in your own Hetzner project. The token is checked, then encrypted.

delete.description: Remove a cloud credential. A linked account is also revoked at the provider.

get.description:
Regions and sizes this cloud account can create a server in, loaded from
the provider (DigitalOcean) and kept for ten minutes. Other providers answer
422 catalog_not_available; type their size instead.

post.description:
Link a Google Cloud project (ADR 0024). Returns gcloud commands that
create a service account with an id made for this link, give it a custom
role limited to Compute Engine, and let Odotify's service account act as
it. Run them in your project, then send the project id to
PUT /cloud/gcp/{credential_id}. Odotify never holds a key of yours.

get.description: The setup commands of a Google Cloud link again, to finish or redo it.

put.description:
Send the id of the project you ran the commands in. Odotify acts as the
service account once to check it, then the project can be used to create
servers.

post.description:
Link a cloud account over OAuth (DigitalOcean). Send the browser to the
returned URL; the provider sends it back to the dashboard, which completes
the link with POST /v1/cloud/oauth/complete. Valid for 15 minutes.

get.description:
What can be created: locations allowed by the organization's data
residency, the sizes Odotify provides, and the organization's own credentials.

Check that the audit log is complete and unaltered: the hash chain of
every event, and the signed chain heads Odotify records every hour.

The organization's evidence for its own audits (SOC 2, ISO 27001):
who has access, API keys and their age, backup success, restore drills
with their certificates, open alerts and the audit log's integrity.
External PostgreSQL clusters the organization's instances can use.

post.description:
Register an external PostgreSQL (FR-INS-013): Amazon RDS or Aurora,
Cloud SQL, Azure, a provider's managed database, or a primary with
standbys. The password is kept encrypted and reaches only the servers
whose instances use the cluster. Check it from a server before use.

delete.description: Forget a cluster no instance uses. The cluster itself is not touched.

patch.description:
Change how the cluster is reached, or rotate its password. Check it
again afterwards: that sends the change to the server.

post.description:
Connect to every host of the cluster from one of your servers: which
host takes writes, its version, and whether the server's PostgreSQL client
can back it up.

Approve and run a proposed change. Dashboard sessions only: API keys and
assistants can propose, never approve.

delete.description:
Stop using the organization's email provider. Odotify's mail server is
removed from every production instance; mail servers added in Odoo stay.

get.description: The email provider the organization's Odoo instances send through.

put.description:
Save the organization's email provider (Mailgun, Postmark, Amazon SES or
any SMTP server) and set it as the outgoing mail server of every production
instance. Odoo uses it at once, and instances created later get it too.
The password or token is kept encrypted and never returned.

post.description:
Send a test email through the saved provider from one of the
organization's servers, the way its Odoo instances send. A blocked port or
a refused login comes back as the error.

delete.description:
Forget the Enterprise access. Enterprise instances keep running the
addons they have; new ones, and copies of them, need access again.

get.description:
Whether the organization has Odoo Enterprise access: a GitHub token,
uploaded packages, or both.

put.description:
Save the organization's Odoo Enterprise access (FR-INS-003).

Odotify does not resell Enterprise. Give a GitHub token of an account Odoo
has given access to odoo/enterprise (Odoo partners and Odoo.sh customers
have it); it is checked with GitHub before it is saved, and kept sealed.
The subscription code, if given, is registered in each Enterprise database.

post.description:
Upload the Odoo Enterprise package for one Odoo major (ADR 0025).

For customers without access to odoo/enterprise on GitHub: download the
Enterprise .deb (or the source .tar.gz) for the version from
odoo.com/page/download, start an upload here, PUT the file to the returned
link, then call markEnterprisePackageUploaded. Servers keep only the
Enterprise modules from it. A newer upload for the same major replaces the
older one; instances already running keep the modules they have.

delete.description:
Remove an uploaded package. Instances keep the Enterprise modules they
already have.

post.description:
Say the upload finished. Odotify checks the file arrived, at its size,
and puts it in use for its Odoo major.

Accept the Odoo Enterprise terms for the organization (ADR 0033): you
confirm it holds a valid Odoo Enterprise subscription, from Odoo S.A. or an
Odoo partner, that covers every database it runs on Enterprise here. Once
accepted, the Enterprise packages Odotify shares can be used. Owners and
admins only, signed in to the dashboard. Who accepted, when and which
version are kept and written to the audit log.

Bring a database from Odoo.sh, Odoo Online or your own server (FR-INS-005).

Download a backup from the source's database manager as a zip with the
filestore (or a pg_dump custom-format `.dump`), then either upload it with
the returned link or give a link the server can download it from. Then
create an instance with this import's id. Versions are checked before
anything is restored: the database must be from the same Odoo major as the
new instance. An Enterprise database needs the organization's Enterprise
access, and then runs on Enterprise.
Say the upload finished. Odotify checks the file arrived, at its size.

Save what new instances start with (FR-TPL-001). Create an instance from
it with `template_id` on POST /instances.

put.description: Make it the template the dashboard picks first (FR-TPL-002).

post.description:
Create an Odoo instance on an active server (FR-INV-001).

Returns 202 with the creation job and the initial admin password, which is
shown only in this response. The instance gets a platform subdomain with a
TLS certificate and the default backup schedule (daily, keep seven).

delete.description:
Delete an instance and everything it has, in any state but creating
(FR-INS-016): container, database, files, backups, certificates and its
platform DNS record. Type the instance's name to confirm. Not reversible.

get.description:
The modules uploaded to the instance and their state in Odoo, read live
from the server.

post.description:
Upload a zip of one or more Odoo modules (each a folder with a
__manifest__.py), up to 200 MB. PUT the zip to the returned link, then call
installAddonUpload.

Install an uploaded zip. A backup is required first: take one in the
job (backup_first, the default), or confirm one exists. The server dumps
the database again just before installing; if Odoo fails, the previous
modules and database come back.

delete.description:
Delete an uploaded module's files from the server. Only a module that
is not installed: uninstall it in Odoo's Apps first.

post.description: Add a schedule (FR-BAK-001). Keep either a number of backups or of days.

delete.description: Stop a schedule. Its existing backups stay until deleted.

post.description: Take an on-demand backup now (FR-BAK-005). Kept until deleted by hand.

delete.description: Delete a backup's archive from the server and its destination (FR-BAK-016).

post.description:
A short-lived link to download one backup archive from managed storage
(FR-WLB-003). Every download is written to the audit log.

Restore a backup into this instance or into a new one (FR-BAK-014, FR-BAK-015).

Restoring over this instance replaces its database and files. It is only
possible from the dashboard, needs the instance's name typed to confirm, and
takes a safety backup first; the old data is kept until the restored instance
answers, and put back if anything fails.

Run a restore drill of this backup now (ADR 0017).

The server restores it into a scratch database beside the instance, checks
that Odoo loads it with the code the instance runs and that every
attachment's file is there, then drops the copy. The instance keeps running
throughout. A drill that passes earns a signed certificate.

Move the instance's database onto an external cluster, to another one,
or back onto its server. Odoo stops while the database is copied; if it
does not start on the copy, it starts again where it was.

Propose an index, built online with CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY
(FR-DBO-010). It waits for approval in the dashboard (FR-DBO-012), unless a
person with approval rights sets approve from the dashboard.

Propose dropping an index with DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY. The result keeps
the exact SQL to recreate it (FR-DBO-011). Constraint indexes are refused.

Add your own domain (FR-DOM-001). Point an A record at the server first:
Odotify checks DNS, then requests the certificate. Names that do not point
here yet wait, and each shows what to change.
Check DNS again and request certificates for names that now point here.

patch.description: Make a domain primary, or make it redirect to the primary (FR-DOM-004).

post.description:
Move a Community instance onto Odoo Enterprise.

The server downloads Enterprise with the organization's access, dumps the
database, installs web_enterprise and restarts Odoo; if anything fails it
restores the dump and stays on Community. There is no way back to
Community from here: that means uninstalling Enterprise modules and their
data, which is left to Odoo itself.

put.description:
Apply the rules on the instance's server: nginx checks them and reloads
within seconds. Refused, with nothing changed, if nginx rejects them.

get.description: The request log, newest first. Kept 14 days.

parameters.description: allowed, blocked, or one reason (ip, country, path, bot, rate_limit...)
parameters.name: verdict

schema.description: allowed, blocked, or one reason (ip, country, path, bot, rate_limit...)
schema.title: Verdict

get.description: The filtered log as CSV, newest first, up to 50,000 rows.

parameters.description: allowed, blocked, or one reason (ip, country, path, bot, rate_limit...)
parameters.name: verdict

schema.description: allowed, blocked, or one reason (ip, country, path, bot, rate_limit...)
schema.title: Verdict

get.description: Allowed and blocked requests per day. Counts are exact.
The instance's status history: each problem it had and when it cleared.

Live statements, idle transactions and lock waits from the last refresh
(FR-DBO-007). Refresh with kinds=["activity"] for a current view.

Unused, duplicate and invalid indexes, foreign keys without a supporting
index, and tables read mostly by sequential scans (FR-DBO-008).

One index's last checked status (FR-DBO-009); 404 until it was checked
with a refresh naming the index.

A statement's generic plan (FR-DBO-006); 404 until it was planned with a
refresh naming the queryid. Planning never runs the statement.

post.description:
Ask the agent for a fresh report, a statement's plan or an index's status.
Returns a job; when it succeeds, read the report again.

get.description:
The slow-query report from pg_stat_statements (FR-DBO-004), as the agent
last reported it. Query text is normalized and every literal is redacted on
the server, so no business data is included (FR-DBO-005).

post.description:
A single-use link that signs the browser into the instance's Odoo as
the chosen user, without their password. It expires after a minute and
every link issued is in the audit log.

get.description:
The instance's active internal Odoo users, read live from its database
through the server's agent, to choose whom to log in as.

Compare a staging copy with its production instance, live from their
servers: staging's Git commit, the uploaded addons and the Odoo apps
installed. Data is never compared or pushed.

post.description:
Push the chosen changes to production as one job: a backup of
production first, then the commit, the addons and the apps. Each step
puts production back if Odoo fails. Refused if anything changed since the
preview whose fingerprint is sent.

Replace a staging copy's data with a fresh, neutralized copy of production
(FR-STG-004). Type the staging instance's name to confirm.

delete.description: Disconnect the repository. The deployed code keeps running.

put.description:
Connect a Git repository of custom addons (FR-GIT-001).

Add the returned public key as a read-only deploy key, and the webhook URL with
the secret (shown once) to the repository's push webhooks: GitHub sends it as
the signing secret, GitLab as the token.

How often the newest backup is restored in a drill: weekly, monthly (the
default for production instances) or off.

post.description:
Make a staging copy of a production instance (FR-STG-001).

The copy is restored from a fresh backup of production and neutralized before
it starts: outgoing mail, scheduled actions and payment providers are off.

Test an upgrade to the next Odoo major (FR-INS-017).

Odotify makes a neutralized staging copy of production, reports what
happens to every installed module and upgrades the copy with OCA's
OpenUpgrade. Production is untouched until someone promotes the upgrade.
Odoo Enterprise databases are upgraded by Odoo S.A. instead.

delete.description:
Close an upgrade that will not be promoted. Its staging copy stays
until you delete it.

post.description:
Upgrade production the way the test upgraded its copy. Production is
backed up first, and any failure puts back its database and the previous
major. Only from the dashboard, with the instance's name typed.

Invite someone by email with a pre-selected role and scope (FR-ACC-004).

Returns 202 with the job that sends the email; the invitation expires after
the configured time to live.

get.description: A job with its steps, timings and, on failure, the reason and the fix (FR-SRV-029).

delete.description: Remove a member. Destructive: reachable only from a signed-in dashboard session.

patch.description: Change a member's role or scope. An organization always keeps at least one owner.

get.description:
Instances this organization lends to partners, the ones it borrows, and
the code a partner needs to share instances with it (FR-ACC-006).

post.description:
Lend named instances to a partner organization with a role (operator,
developer or viewer). Its members get that role on those instances, never
more than their own role at the partner. Nothing is copied or moved.

delete.description: Take the access back. It ends on the partner's next request.

post.description:
Attach an existing Ubuntu or Debian server over SSH (FR-SRV-011).

Odotify logs in with the organization's attach key before answering. If it
cannot log in or become root, the request fails with `ssh_key_refused`,
`ssh_unreachable`, `sudo_needs_password` or `host_key_changed`, and
`details.remedy` says what to change. Otherwise it returns 202 with the
provisioning job (preflight, baseline, agent).

Create a cloud server and provision it (FR-SRV-010).

With `offer_id`, Odotify provides the server (Hetzner) and bills it monthly
with your subscription. With `credential_id` and `server_type`, it is created
in that cloud account of yours (Hetzner, DigitalOcean, Vultr, Akamai, AWS, Google
Cloud or Azure)
and the provider bills you. Returns 202 with the job.

delete.description:
Detach a server with no instances. An attached host is left untouched
(204). A server Odotify created at a cloud provider is destroyed and its
billing stops: that runs as a job (202 with `job_id`).

post.description:
Install the newest agent release on the server. The agent checks the
download against the release's SHA-256, replaces itself and restarts; the
job finishes when it reports the new version. Instances keep running.

Propose PostgreSQL parameter changes. A person approves them by typing
the server's name; changes needing a restart say so.

get.description:
Server-wide blocks, automatic bans and the host firewall (ufw), as the
agent last reported them (about once a minute).

CPU, memory, disk, network and PostgreSQL connections over a time range,
from the agent's one-minute samples (kept 30 days). Longer ranges come in
larger buckets: 1 minute for 1h, up to 4 hours for 30d.
The tunable PostgreSQL parameters as the agent last reported them (FR-DBO-001).

post.description:
Change PostgreSQL parameters (FR-DBO-002). Changes that need a restart are
refused with 409 unless confirm_restart is set; a value PostgreSQL rejects, or
one it cannot start with, is undone.
Run provisioning again after fixing what the failed job reported.

Add an endpoint (FR-API-011). Each request is signed:
`Odotify-Signature: t=<unix>,v1=<hex HMAC-SHA256 of "<t>.<body>">` with the
signing secret returned here once. Failed deliveries are retried for about a day.

get.description: The event types an endpoint can subscribe to.
The latest 50 deliveries, newest first.

post.description: Send a past event again, with the same event id.
Queue a `ping` event to the endpoint.
